Unofficial until approved by the
  Alhambra City Council

  MINUTES
  Regular Meeting
  ALHAMBRA CITY COUNCIL
  October 9, 2023
  6:00 p.m.

ROLL CALL: At 6:05 p.m., on Monday, October 9, 2023, the Alhambra City Council met in the Council
Chambers of Alhambra City Hall

PRESENT:  ANDRADE-STADLER, LEE, MALONEY, PÉREZ, MAZA
ABSENT:  NONE

Officials Present in person and via Zoom: City Manager Binnquist, City Attorney Montes, Assistant
City Manager Garcia, Deputy City Manager Stover, City Clerk Myles, Director of Finance Lieu, Director
of Parks and Recreation Macias, Director of Library LohGuan, Director of Community Development
Ho, Director of Human Resources Ko, Chief of Police Kennedy

FLAG SALUTE:  Led by Mayor Maza

LAND ACKNOWLEDGEMENT: We acknowledged that the land on which we are gathered is the
traditional, ancestral, and unceded territory of the Gabrielino/Tongva peoples. We seek to prioritize
respect for the historic culture and contemporary presence of the native peoples throughout California,
especially in the greater Los Angeles/Alhambra area. We come with respect and gratitude for the
Gabrielino/Tongva people who still consider themselves the caretakers of this land. It is through their
examples that we are reminded of our greater responsibility to take care of Mother Earth and to take
care of each other.

READING OF ORDINANCE TITLES

Government Code Section 36934 requires that all ordinances be read in full prior to City Council taking
action on the ordinance. By listing the ordinance title on the Council agenda, Council may determine
that the title has been read.

Action Taken: By motion, determined that the titles to all ordinances which appear on this public
agenda have been read, and waived further reading.

  Vote:  Moved:  PÉREZ  Seconded:  ANDRADE-STADLER
  Ayes:  ANDRADE-STADLER, MALONEY, LEE, PÉREZ, MAZA
  Noes:  NONE
  Absent:  NONE

MAZA: Mayor MAZA requested to move Item No. 2 and the Consent Calendar ahead of Item No. 1.
There were no objections.

PUBLIC HEARING

1.  CONSIDERATION OF THE READOPTION OF DRAFT 4 OF THE 2021-2029 HOUSING
  ELEMENT OF THE ALHAMBRA GENERAL PLAN, AND DIRECTING STAFF TO
  RESUBMIT THE DRAFT HOUSING ELEMENT TO THE STATE DEPARTMENT OF
  HOUSING AND COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT – F2M20-37, N2M23-116, R2M23-50

  1
10-9-23
   This was the time and place set by Notice No. N2M23-116 for the City Council to hold a public
  hearing to consider the readoption of Draft 4 of the 2021-2029 Housing Element of the
  Alhambra General Plan and to direct staff to resubmit the Draft Housing Element to the State
  Department of Housing and Community Development. Director of Community Development
  HO and Chris BLAKNEY, ECONorthwest, delivered a staff report, a copy of which is on file in
  the City Clerk’s Office. On October 5, 2021, the Housing Element was submitted to the State
  Department of Housing and Community Development “HCD”. City staff and the City’s
  Consultant (ECONorthwest) worked on responding to HCD’s multiple correction letters and
  resubmitted updated versions of the Housing Element based on HCD’s comments. On January
  3, 2022, the Planning Commission conducted a public hearing and recommended that the
  Alhambra City Council adopt the 2021-2029 Draft Housing Element (“Housing Element”).
  Then, on January 31, 2022, the City Council adopted the Housing Element and directed staff
  to resubmit it to HCD for formal review. After submitting the adopted Housing Element to HCD,
  the City received multiple correction letters dated, December 2, 2021; April 8, 2022; October
  10, 2022; and May 25, 2023. On May 25, 2023, HCD issued the City a letter indicating that
  this most recent 4th Draft of the Housing Element (attached to the staff report) met the statutory
  requirements of State Housing Element Law. However, HCD indicated that the Housing
  Element could not be found in substantial compliance until the City completed the necessary
  re-zoning, which was currently underway as part of the comprehensive Zoning Code update.
  Given that changes were made since the Planning Commission and City Council approved
  the Housing Element in January 2022, HCD required re-adoption of the Housing Element. All
  revisions that occurred since the City Council approved the Housing Element in January 2022
  were shown in the redlined version of the Draft Housing Element provided in the staff report,
  and a clean, non-redlined version was provided as an attachment to the staff report as well.
  On August 7, 2023, the Planning Commission conducted a public hearing on the re-adoption
  of the 4th Draft of the 2021-2029 Housing Element, and then continued the item to their
  meetings on August 21, 2023 and September 18, 2023. On September 18, 2023, the Planning
  Commission finalized a list of recommendations for nine (9) additional revisions to the 4th Draft
  of the Housing Element which were outlined in an attachment to the staff report and adopted
  a Resolution recommending the City Council re-adopt the revised 2021-2029 Housing
  Element. All comment letters received prior to this meeting as well as additional documentation
  related to the Housing Element have been posted on the project website at
  www.alhambrahousingelement.com and were available for public review.

  Public Comment:
  1) Lewis MCCAMMON, 105 N. Cordova St., thanked Mr. Blakney and staff for their hard work on
  the housing element, expressed support for the Planning Commission’s recommendations, and
  the changes to help protect the current and future residents of the City.

  2) Henry FONG, via Zoom, noted that HCD would require additional analysis for Planning
  Commission’s recommendation on item A, E, and H and expressed concern with the amount
  of time and money that was spent by the City on updating the housing element.

  3) Melissa MICHELSON, via Zoom, noted that residents in Alhambra were following along with
  the Planning Commission during this whole process, noted concerns with the Villages and
  building on contaminated land, and noted that the updated housing element would satisfy the
  City’s RHNA requirements,

  4) Jennifer NG, via Zoom, reiterated the comments by Mr. McCammon and noted that the City
  should not be building housing on superfund sites.

  5) Olga ALARID, via Zoom, expressed opposition to developers who were proposing multi-level
  housing.

  6) Marisol GRIER, via Zoom, stated the needs of the community should be reflected in the housing
  element, expressed concern with proposed 75-foot building height limit in the housing element,
  2
10-9-23
   and stated the Council should adopt the housing element with the recommendations from the
  Planning Commission.

  7) Ari Guiterrez ARAMBULA, via Zoom, stated that the City did not need 75-foot market rate
  condos in the City, expressed support for the Planning Commission’s recommendations for
  the housing element, noted that more housing would mean additional need public transit, and
  expressed support for an additional gateway in the City.

  Discussion: Vice Mayor PÉREZ inquired about the historical background and engagement
  from the Department of Housing and Community Development (HCD) throughout the housing
  element review process and Mr. BLAKNEY responded to questions.

  Councilmember MALONEY thanked the Planning Commission and public for participating in
  the process thus far, inquired if the City could legally meet all the needed requirements if they
  adopted the recommendations made by the Planning Commission, expressed concern with
  housing projects mixed with commercial projects, noted the height limits for buildings need to
  be discussed further, and inquired about the potential liability of housing projects on
  contaminated sites. City Attorney MONTES responded to questions.

  Councilmember LEE noted that the Council needed to take their time reviewing the housing
  element, discussed the flexible zoning options, proposed that the Council entertain flexible
  zoning in certain parts of the City, inquired if there would be any additional properties added
  to the sites inventory, and Mr. HO, Mr. MONTES, and Mr. BLAKNEY responded to questions.

  Councilmember ANDRADE-STADLER expressed appreciation for the affordable housing in
  the proposed housing element, discussed potential housing at the Village property, suggested
  sending a letter to Congresswoman Judy Chu’s office requesting research by the
  Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) of the contaminated land by the Villages, and
  expressed support for the proposed housing element with the nine recommended changes by
  the Planning Commission.

  Mayor MAZA discussed the importance of local control and noted that HCD has strict
  regulations, inquired if HCD would approve the City’s housing element if the Council removed
  sites with contaminated concerns, inquired about adding the Wondries Ford property to the
  site inventory, inquired if the HCD commented on the Villages property, inquired if nearby
  houses by the Villages could have difficulty making improvements if they were also on
  contaminated land, inquired if any other municipalities were in lawsuits over building housing
  on contaminated land, noted that height concerns for buildings would be discussed at a later
  date, and Director of Community Development HO, City Attorney MONTES, and Mr.
  BLAKNEY responded to questions.

  Councilmember ANDRADE-STADLER provided historical context of businesses dumping
  contaminated materials, discussed the site of the Villages development for housing, and
  reiterated her request to send a letter to Congresswoman Judy Chu’s office regarding the
  contaminated land.

  Mayor MAZA discussed the importance of improving Valley Blvd. and avoiding builder’s
  remedy.

  Vice Mayor PÉREZ noted that the 75-foot height requirement would be addressed when the
  zoning code went before the Council and expressed support for the recommendations made
  by the Planning Commission.

  Councilmember LEE discussed historical district sites in the City, discussed including
  language for flexible zoning in the housing element, and Mr. HO responded to questions.

  3
10-9-23
   The Council discussed the potential rezoning of Valley Blvd. and how current businesses on
  that street would be affected.

RECESS & RECONVENE:  Mayor MAZA called for a brief recess at 9:23 p.m. and the meeting
resumed with all Councilmembers present at 9:30 p.m.

  Councilmember ANDRADE-STADLER inquired if adopting the housing element would prevent
  future builder’s remedy. City Attorney MONTES provided clarification.

  Councilmember MALONEY made a motion to support the recommendations by Planning
  Commission with the exception of the recommendations that HCD expressed concern about
  which included A, C, E, and H(b) and directed staff to go out to RFP for a consultant to assist
  with an RPD process that would be compliant with State law, look at an incentive program for
  commercial uses on the ground floor of mixed-use developments, and have a deeper
  discussion amongst the Council regarding the super-fund area.

  The Council discussed HCD’s recommendation to remove the RPD permitting process and
  Mr. BLAKNEY and City Attorney MONTES responded to questions.

  Councilmember ANDRADE-STADLER stated that Mr. Blakney should have notified the City
  earlier of HCD’s concerns and assisted the City with a remedy that would have been compliant
  with HCD’s standards.

  Councilmember LEE expressed concern with HCD’s comments pertaining to historic
  preservation and Mr. BLAKNEY provided clarification.

  Mayor MAZA clarified that if the City did not remove the RPD permitting process, the housing
  element would not be approved by HCD. Mr. BLAKNEY noted HCD was not averse to a
  process but it needed to be a process with objective criteria.

  The Council discussed the Planning Commission’s recommendation regarding the City’s RPD
  permitting process and potential modifications to the process to adhere to HCD’s standards.

  Councilmember LEE offered an amendment to the motion to keep recommendation A and to
  revise the current RPD process in order to get the housing element approved.

  Councilmember MALONEY expressed concern with the amendment to the motion and noted
  that he supported recommendation A but was concerned that HCD would not approve the
  housing element with that recommendation.

  Councilmember ANDRADE-STADLER reiterated her concerns with the environmental
  concerns with building on contaminated land.

  Mayor MAZA reiterated his concerns with builder’s remedy.

  Councilmember MALONEY reiterated concern with the amendment to the motion and noted
  that it left the City open to potential builder’s remedy.

  The Council discussed leaving recommendation A in the motion or removing it from the motion
  and revising the current RPD process.

  City Attorney MONTES stated the Council could add additional language that would exempt
  statutory by-right projects, evaluate projects based on objectives standards, that are to be
  determined, and to confirm appropriate CEQA regulations undertaken by the projects.

  4
10-9-23
   Mr. BLAKNEY recommended removing recommendation A and revising the language that
  states the removal of the RPD process with language that stated the City would put out an
  RFP to hire a consultant to re-establish the RPD process with objective criteria.

  Councilmember LEE accepted the language proposed by Mr. Blakney as her friendly
  amendment to the motion. Councilmember MALONEY accepted the amendment to the
  motion.

  Action Taken:  City Council:

  1. Adopted Resolution No. R2M23-50 entitled: A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL
  OF THE CITY OF ALHAMBRA, CALIFORNIA, APPROVING GENERAL PLAN
  AMENDMENT GPA-22-01 READOPTING THE 2021-2029 HOUSING ELEMENT OF THE
  ALHAMBRA GENERAL PLAN (DRAFT 4), AND DIRECTING STAFF TO SUBMIT THE
  READOPTED HOUSING ELEMENT TO THE STATE OF CALIFORNIA DEPARTMENT
  OF HOUSING AND COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT FOR CERTIFICATION

  2. Removed Planning Commission Recommendation A and revised the language that stated
  the removal of the RPD process with language that stated the City would put out an RFP
  to hire a consultant to re-establish the RPD process with objective material.

  Vote:  Moved:  MALONEY  Seconded:  LEE
  Ayes:  ANDRADE-STADLER, LEE, MALONEY, PÉREZ, MAZA
  Noes:  NONE
  Absent:  NONE

PRESENTATION

2.  LEGISLATIVE UPDATE: SB 567 (DURAZO) ON TENANT PROTECTIONS AND SB2 ON
  STRENGTHENING CONCEALED GUN WEAPON LAWS AND FIREARM POSESSION
  RESTRICTIONS – F2M23-7, O2M23-4820

  Assistant City Manager GARCIA delivered a staff report. On September 11, 2023, staff
  presented a report advising that SB 567 (Durazo), which added requirements and restrictions
  for evictions related to substantial remodels, passed the Senate and then was awaiting the
  Assembly for Third Reading. On September 30, 2023, SB 567 was officially signed by the
  Governor, resulting the bill be enacted into law; however, pursuant to any last-minute
  amendments that occurred during the Third Reading process. One key change to the bill was
  a new implementation date of April 1, 2024. On May 23, 2023, the City Council adopted
  Urgency Ordinance O2M23-4811, establishing the same renoviction protections as SB 567
  through December 31, 2023. SB 567 was originally identified to become effective on January
  1, 2024; however, since this date was recently amended to April 1, 2024, staff requested the
  City’s Urgency Ordinance be extended to March 31, 2024 to ensure there were no gaps in
  protections in Alhambra before SB 567 would become effective.

  On September 26, 2023, the Governor signed various firearm safety bills, including SB 2,
  which was designed to strengthen concealed carry weapons laws by ensuring firearms in
  public do not pose danger; setting minimum age requirements to 21; requiring stronger storage
  and training requirements; identifying certain sensitive places where guns may not be carried;
  and including due process protections. On September 25, 2023, the City Council introduced
  and gave first reading to Ordinance O2M23-4820, prohibiting firearms on public property.
  Since SB 2, under Section 27, addressed those same sensitive place and restrictions as
  Ordinance O2M23-4820, staff recommended the City not proceed with agendizing the second
  reading of Ordinance O2M23-4820.
  5
10-9-23
   Public Comment:

  1) Brian OTIS spoke in favor of SB 567 and requested the Council to revisit the moratorium
  in April.

  2) Andy O’BRIEN, via Zoom, expressed concern with stricter gun laws in the City.

  Discussion:  Councilmember LEE noted that she was in favor of extending the
  urgency ordinance until March 31, 2024, expressed support for SB 567, clarified the intent of
  SB 2 and inquired how the Police Department would implement the law if it were to pass. City
  Attorney MONTES responded to questions.

  Councilmember ANDRADE-STADLER inquired if SB 2 and SB 567 overlapped with the City’s
  current ordinances. City Attorney MONTES provided clarification.

  Vice Mayor PÉREZ thanked Senator Durazo for her work on SB 567 and thanked Senator
  Portantino for his work on SB 2, referenced the last public comment and noted that racist
  comments were unacceptable.

  Councilmember MALONEY reiterated the thoughts of the Council and expressed support for
  extending the urgency ordinance.

  Mayor MAZA expressed support for extending the urgency ordinance and the progression of
  SB 2.

  Action Taken:  City Council received a report regarding the passage of SB 567
  (Durazo), state tenant protections subject to “no fault” evictions due to substantial remodels,
  which has relevance to Alhambra’s Urgency Ordinance O2M23-4811, which expires on
  December 31, 2023, but should be extended to March 31, 2024; received a report on SB 2
  (Portantino), which bill was recently signed into law prohibiting possessing firearms in public
  property, as intended by the City Council under Ordinance O2M23-4820; and, directed staff to
  undertake the steps necessary to carry out the Council’s actions.

CONSENT AGENDA (Item Nos. 3-15)

All other items listed under the Consent Agenda were considered by the City Council to be routine
and were enacted by one motion.

3.  AWARD CONTRACT: 6th STREET SEWER MAIN REPLACEMENT PROJECT- PHASE II –
  F2M21-47, N2M23-103, C2M23-79, M2M23-172

  On August 28, 2023, the City Council approved the distribution of a Notice Inviting Bids for the
  Sixth Street Sewer Main – Phase 2 between San Marino Avenue and Valley Boulevard. On
  September 28, 2023, bids were opened by the City Clerk. Ten bids were received, which
  ranged from $1,168,950.00 to $2,667,640.00. Ramona Inc. submitted the lowest qualified bid
  at $1,168,950.00. Staff reviewed the bid submitted by Ramona Inc. and found it to be in full
  compliance and conformance with the project specifications.

  Discussion:  None

  Action Taken:  City Council awarded a contract, subject to final language approval by
  the City Manager and City Attorney, by and between the City of Alhambra and Ramona Inc.,
  for the Sixth Street Sewer Main Replacement Project - Phase 2 in an amount not to exceed

  6
10-9-23
   $1,168,950.00; found the 6th Street Sewer Main Replacement Project - Phase 2 categorically
  exempt from California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) pursuant to CEQA Guidelines
  Section 15301 (b); and, directed staff to undertake the steps necessary to finalize Council’s
  action. (M2M23-172)

  Vote:  Moved:  PÉREZ  Seconded:  MALONEY
  Ayes:  MALONEY, LEE, ANDRADE-STADLER, PÉREZ, MAZA
  Noes:  NONE
  Absent:  NONE

4.  AWARD CONTRACT: REHABILITATION OF THE SEWER MAIN ON BEACON STREET –
  F2M23-61, N2M23-104, C2M23-80, M2M23-173

  On August 28, 2023, the City Council approved the distribution of a Notice Inviting Bids for the
  Rehabilitation of the Sewer Main on Beacon Street. On September 21, 2023, bids were opened
  by the City Clerk. Three bids were received, which ranged from $36,560.00 to $111,980.00.
  Southwest Pipeline & Trenchless Corp. submitted the lowest qualified bid at $36,560.00. Staff
  reviewed the bid submitted by Southwest Pipeline & Trenchless Corp. and found it to be in full
  compliance and conformance with the project specifications.

  Discussion:  None

  Action Taken:  City Council awarded a contract, subject to final language approval by
  the City Manager and City Attorney, by and between the City of Alhambra and Southwest
  Pipeline & Trenchless Corp. for the Rehabilitation of the Sewer Main on Beacon Street in an
  amount not to exceed $36,560.00; found the Rehabilitation of the Sewer Main on Beacon
  Street categorically exempt from California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) pursuant to
  CEQA Guidelines Section 15301 (b); and, directed staff to undertake the steps necessary to
  finalize Council’s action. (M2M23-173)

  Vote:  Moved:  PÉREZ  Seconded:  MALONEY
  Ayes:  MALONEY, LEE, ANDRADE-STADLER, PÉREZ, MAZA
  Noes:  NONE
  Absent:  NONE

5.  NOTICE OF COMPLETION: REHABILITATION OF THE  STORM  DRAIN  ON
  MONTEZUMA AVENUE – F2M23-40, C2M23-49, M2M23-174

  On June 26, 2023, the City Council awarded a contract to Sancon Technologies, Inc. for the
  Rehabilitation of the Storm Drain on Montezuma Avenue in an amount of $130,045.00. There
  was one change order authorized for the project, which was for additional work to CCTV the
  storm drain downstream of the project area on Ramona Avenue. The change order increased
  the total amount of the contract by $1,250.00, for a total of $131,295.00. The project was
  completed in accordance with the City requirements and specifications. As such, it was
  appropriate for the City Council to accept the project as complete and instruct the City Clerk
  that the Notice of Completion be filed with the County of Los Angeles Recorder’s Office.

  Discussion:  None

  Action Taken:  City Council accepted the work of Sancon Technologies, Inc. for the
  Rehabilitation of the Storm Drain on Montezuma Avenue as complete in the amount of
  $131,295.00; directed the Finance Director to appropriate $1,250.00 from the Safe Clean
  Water Program Fund balance and allocate the fund to account number 233.80.8882.92240;
  7
10-9-23
   directed the City Clerk to file a Notice of Completion with the County of Los Angeles for
  recordation; directed the Finance Director to release the five percent retention 35 days from
  the date of recordation if no liens are filed; and, directed staff to undertake the steps necessary
  to finalize Council’s action. (M2M23-174)

  Vote:  Moved:  PÉREZ  Seconded:  MALONEY
  Ayes:  MALONEY, LEE, ANDRADE-STADLER, PÉREZ, MAZA
  Noes:  NONE
  Absent:  NONE

6.  NOTICE INVITING BIDS: ALHAMBRA PARK POOL IMPROVEMENT PROJECT – F2M22-
  37, N2M23-121

  On October 24, 2022, the City Council awarded a contract to Goodale Architecture and
  Planning for professional engineering and design services to provide plans, specifications, and
  bid documentation for the Alhambra Pool Improvement Project. The Alhambra Park Pool
  Improvement Project would include a complete renovation of the pool facility to transform the
  lobby, expand restrooms and changing areas, upgrade to high efficiency fixtures, install new
  roofing and exterior upgrades, sustainable landscaping, and shaded seating. Specifications
  and bid documentation were completed for the Project. Bids would be due no later than 10:30
  a.m. on December 7, 2023 in the office of the City Clerk and would be opened at 11:00 a.m.
  that same day.

  Discussion:  None

  Action Taken:  City Council authorized staff to circulate a Notice Inviting Bids to
  prospective contractors for the Alhambra Park Pool Improvement Project; and, directed staff
  to undertake the steps necessary to finalize Council’s action.

  Vote:  Moved:  PÉREZ  Seconded:  MALONEY
  Ayes:  MALONEY, LEE, ANDRADE-STADLER, PÉREZ, MAZA
  Noes:  NONE
  Absent:  NONE

7.  ACCEPT GRANT: SAN GABRIEL VALLEY COUNCIL OF GOVERNMENTS (SGVCOG)
  FOR HOMELESS SERVICES – F2M23-18, M2M23-175

  The SGVCOG entered into a contract with the County of Los Angeles for Measure H funding
  for homeless services in support of the County’s Homeless Initiative (HI) strategies to combat
  homelessness in the San Gabriel Valley. The SGVCOG Board allocated $30,000 from
  Measure H funds to support Alhambra’s needs, including supplementing existing
  homelessness programs, outreach and services for hard-to-reach populations. The City and
  SGVCOG have set the terms of ongoing collaboration with respect to addressing
  homelessness in a Memorandum of Agreement (MOA). The term of this MOA is through June
  30, 2024, and it may be extended by mutual agreement of both parties by way of an
  amendment to the MOA.

  Discussion:  None

  Action Taken:  City Council authorized staff to accept the San Gabriel Valley Council
  of Governments (SGVCOG) grant in the amount of $30,000 for homeless outreach, housing
  navigator and case management services and emergency housing/shelter placement;
  authorized the City Manager to sign the Memorandum of Agreement (MOA); appropriated the
  8
10-9-23
   grant revenue and expenditure funds in the amount of $30,000; and, directed staff to undertake
  the steps necessary to finalize the Council’s action. (M2M23-175)

  Vote:  Moved:  PÉREZ  Seconded:  MALONEY
  Ayes:  MALONEY, LEE, ANDRADE-STADLER, PÉREZ, MAZA
  Noes:  NONE
  Absent:  NONE

8.  AWARD OF CONTRACT:  FINANCIAL CONSULTING SERVICES RELATED TO THE
  AMERICAN RESCUE PLAN ACT - F2M21-67, C2M23-76, M2M23-176

  Staff requested to award a contract to CliftonLarsonAllen LLP to provide financial consulting
  services over the remainder of the ARPA reporting period. The contract would cover four fiscal
  years, ending on June 30, 2027 with a not to exceed amount of $120,000. Federal ARPA funds
  came with stringent guidelines and reporting requirements; consequently, failure to comply
  with the ARPA restrictions and reporting guidelines could result in the recoupment of funds.
  Projects must be obligated by December 31, 2024, with the period of performance concluding
  by December 31, 2026. The City would like to continue services with CliftonLarsonAllen LLP
  due to the firm’s knowledge of the City and for continuity of work product. Staff recommended
  awarding this contract in accordance with Section 3.38.050 of the Alhambra Municipal Code,
  which stipulates the City Council may dispense with the bidding process, at their discretion, if
  they deem it would be advantageous to the City to do so.

  Discussion:  None

  Action Taken:  City Council approved an award of contract, subject to final language
  approval by the City Manager and City Attorney, for professional services with
  CliftonLarsonAllen LLP to provide financial consulting services related to the American Rescue
  Plan Act (ARPA) in the amount of $120,000 (C2M23-76); approve a transfer of $120,000 from
  account number 281.70.9101.92024 to 281.16.9101.62110; and, directed staff to undertake
  the steps necessary to finalize Council’s action. (M2M23-176)

  Vote:  Moved:  PÉREZ  Seconded:  MALONEY
  Ayes:  MALONEY, LEE, ANDRADE-STADLER, PÉREZ, MAZA
  Noes:  NONE
  Absent:  NONE

9.  RESOLUTION APPROVING A THIRD SIDE LETTER AGREEMENT AMENDING THE
  MEMORANDUM OF UNDERSTANDING BETWEEN THE CITY OF ALHAMBRA AND
  ALHAMBRA POLICE DISPATCH ASSOCIATION (APDA) – F2M23-2, R2M23-51, C2M21-
  51, M2M23-179

  In the past few years, the City has been challenged in the area of recruitment and retention of
  Police Dispatchers. Challenges include turnover of newly hired dispatchers who fail to meet
  probationary standards or whom resign or retire. Therefore, staff requested the ability to
  overhire effective immediately. The proposed Third Side Letter with APDA provides the City
  Manager with the ability to overhire by one (1) Full-Time Dispatcher. This ensured the Police
  Department’s staffing levels in this area remain stable by allowing the one overhire position to
  easily and readily be available to step in and fill any vacancies during transition periods brought
  on by any resignations or retirements.

  Discussion:  None

  9
10-9-23
   Action Taken:  City Council, by one motion, took the following actions: 1) Adopted
  Resolution No. R2M23-51 entitled: A Resolution of the Alhambra City Council approving a
  Third Side Letter amending the Memorandum of Understanding between the City of Alhambra
  and the Alhambra Police Dispatch Association; and, 2) Directed the Finance Director to make
  necessary budget adjustments within the Fiscal Year 2023-24 and 2024-25 Adopted Budget
  to allow for the overhire of one (1) Full-Time Dispatcher. (M2M23-179)

  Vote:  Moved:  PÉREZ  Seconded:  MALONEY
  Ayes:  MALONEY, LEE, ANDRADE-STADLER, PÉREZ, MAZA
  Noes:  NONE
  Absent:  NONE

10.  ACCEPT GRANT: STATE OF CALIFORNIA GOVERNOR’S OFFICE OF EMERGENCY
  SERVICES AND THE FEDERAL EMERGENCY MANAGEMENT AGENCY UNDER
  HAZARD MITIGATION GRANT PROGRAM – F2M23-18, M2M23-177

  Staff requested that the City Council City Council accept a grant in the amount of $135,450
  from the State of California Governor’s Office of Emergency Services (Cal OES) and the
  Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA) under the Hazard Mitigation Grant Program
  and approve a related Designation of Applicant’s Agent Resolution. The grant funding would
  be used to create a Local Hazard Mitigation Plan which is a comprehensive, long-term plan

  Board voted to eliminate the SR-710 North extension between Alhambra and Pasadena. The

  support of local road improvements to provide traffic congestion relief within the region. In

  North. Alhambra received an allocation of approximately $241 million for Local Street/Road
  and Freeway Local Interchange Mobility Improvements, Local Street Intersection
  Improvements, and Traffic Signal Synchronization Projects. Currently, the projects were

15.  SECOND READING AND ADOPTION OF AN ORDINANCE REQUIRING SAFE STORAGE
  OF FIREARMS – F2M23-7, O2M23-4819

  At the September 11, 2023 City Council meeting, Vice Mayor Sasha Renée Pérez requested
  that a suite of ordinances recently adopted by the City of Monterey Park be presented to the
  City Council for consideration. At the September 25, 2023 meeting, the Council adopted an
  urgency ordinance to temporarily prohibit the establishment of new firearm sales businesses
  in the City of Alhambra as well as gave first reading to two ordinances related to safe storage
  of firearms and prohibiting firearms on City property. The safe storage ordinance added a new
  section 9.92.050 to the Alhambra Municipal Code entitled “Safe Storage.” The proposed
  ordinance required any person in a residence within the City to store firearms in a locked
  container or disable them with an appropriate safety device in the home. Keeping a firearm
  locked when it is not being carried prevents unauthorized users, including children, from
  accessing and using firearms which can reduce unintentional discharges, firearm theft, and
  suicide.

  Public Comment:
  1) Lola ARMANDARIZ referenced several sections in the proposed ordinance and inquired why
  a copy of the penal code was not included in the staff report and why the California Department
  of Justice roster was not attached to the staff report.

  2) Lewis MCCAMMON, 105 N. Cordova St., expressed support for the proposed ordinance and
  noted guns safety was an important issue.

  3) Jeffrey GOMEZ, 115 Meridian Ave., expressed opposition to the proposed ordinance, noted
  the regulations in the ordinance would do little to increase gun safety, and stated that additional
  education with the public was needed regarding gun safety.

  Discussion:  None

  Action Taken:  City Council, by one motion, declared introduced for its second reading
  and adopted the following ordinance entitled:

  Ordinance No. O2M23-4819: AN ORDINANCE OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE
  CITY OF ALHAMBRA, CALIFORNIA, ADDING SECTION 9.92.050 “SAFE
  STORAGE” TO THE ALHAMBRA MUNICIPAL CODE TO REQUIRE THE SAFE
  STORAGE OF FIREARMS

  Vote:  Moved:  PÉREZ  Seconded:  MALONEY
  Ayes:  MALONEY, LEE, ANDRADE-STADLER, PÉREZ, MAZA
  Noes:  NONE
  Absent:  NONE
